components.name: Consultation Link
components.description: Primary rectangular action used to request a consultation.
components.html: Request a consultation
components.css: .ds-consultation { min-height:48px; display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:16px; padding:12px 24px; background:#315f91; color:#fff; font:600 14px/1.5 Arial,sans-serif; letter-spacing:.025em; text-decoration:none; transition:background-color .3s ease; } .ds-consultation svg { width:20px; height:20px; fill:none; stroke:currentColor; stroke-width:1.75; transition:transform .3s ease; } .ds-consultation:hover { background:#102a43; } .ds-consultation:hover svg { transform:translateX(4px); } .ds-consultation:focus-visible { outline:2px solid currentColor; outline-offset:4px; }

components.name: Primary Navigation
components.description: Quiet inline navigation with an underlined contact action and a hairline baseline.
components.html: AboutTherapyApproachGet in touch
components.css: .ds-nav { display:flex; align-items:center; gap:32px; padding:0 0 20px; border-bottom:1px solid rgba(16,42,67,.15); color:#102a43; font:500 14px/1.5 Arial,sans-serif; } .ds-nav a { color:inherit; text-decoration:none; } .ds-nav a:hover { text-decoration:underline; text-underline-offset:4px; } .ds-nav-action { padding-bottom:4px; border-bottom:1px solid #102a43; } .ds-nav a:focus-visible { outline:2px solid currentColor; outline-offset:4px; }

components.name: FAQ Trigger
components.description: Full-width ruled question row with a plus that becomes a close mark when expanded.
components.css: .ds-faq { width:100%; display:flex; align-items:center; justify-content:space-between; gap:24px; padding:24px 0; border:0; border-bottom:1px solid rgba(16,42,67,.2); background:transparent; color:#102a43; text-align:left; font:500 30px/1.2 Georgia,serif; cursor:pointer; } .ds-faq svg { width:20px; height:20px; flex:none; fill:none; stroke:currentColor; stroke-width:1.75; transition:transform .3s ease; } .ds-faq[aria-expanded="true"] svg { transform:rotate(45deg); } .ds-faq:focus-visible { outline:2px solid currentColor; outline-offset:4px; }

components.name: Photograph Caption
components.description: Paper caption placed directly over the lower edge of an office photograph.
components.css: .ds-photo { position:relative; min-height:360px; margin:0; overflow:hidden; background:#80644c33; } .ds-photo-field { position:absolute; inset:0; background:linear-gradient(135deg,#ccd6df,#9aa9b3); } .ds-photo figcaption { position:absolute; left:0; bottom:0; max-width:310px; padding:24px; background:#fcf9f3; color:rgba(16,42,67,.75); font:400 14px/1.7 Arial,sans-serif; }

narrative.overview:
The system feels like daylight moving across warm plaster, paper, walnut, and a view toward the Pacific. It is editorial rather than spa-like: high-contrast serif statements, a clear humanist sans, rectangular photographs, fine rules, and purposeful areas of open space create calm through composition instead of decorative softness.

The reusable identity is quiet, direct, and materially specific. Pacific Ink carries authority, Restrained Iris marks action, and the warm neutrals hold long-form reading. Real portrait and office photography supply the human presence. The homepage expresses this world through an asymmetric first viewport and alternating light and dark editorial fields; those route-specific arrangements should not become a template for every surface.
keyCharacteristics: Sun-washed warm paper and plaster fields with Pacific Ink typography.
High-contrast Cormorant Garamond statements paired with humanist Manrope copy.
Asymmetric editorial composition, rectangular image crops, and hairline rules.
Restrained iris accents and small walnut details rather than a scattered palette.
Daylight is the only atmospheric motion material.

rules.name: The Morning Room Rule
rules.body: Every surface should feel naturally lit, calm, and composed; warmth comes from material color, photography, and space, never generic wellness decoration.

rules.name: The One Iris Rule
rules.body: Treat iris as a deliberate point of attention, not a color to distribute across every section.

rules.name: The Tonal Field Rule
rules.body: Separate major regions with full fields of paper, plaster, ink, or mist and with fine rules; do not simulate structure with card collections.

rules.name: The Two Voices Rule
rules.body: Serif creates recognition and emotional cadence; sans-serif explains and directs. Do not reverse those jobs or introduce a third type personality.

rules.name: The Asymmetric Pair Rule
rules.body: Pair one dominant element with one supporting element—headline and portrait, image and text, label and content—rather than giving every column equal weight.

rules.name: The Open Floor Rule
rules.body: Use whitespace and hairline divisions to organize information. Avoid boxed modules unless the box is materially meaningful, such as a paper caption laid over a photograph.

rules.name: The Daylight Only Rule
rules.body: Atmospheric motion must read as changing daylight; do not add floating objects, parallax layers, pulsing ornaments, or perpetual ambient loops.

rules.name: The Unsoftened Edge Rule
rules.body: Preserve square corners and straight crops. Rounded wellness cards, pills, and blob masks contradict the system.

rules.name: The Row, Not Card Rule
rules.body: Repeated information belongs in divided editorial rows or open columns, not isolated raised cards.

dos: Do use full tonal fields, asymmetrical columns, and hairline rules to establish hierarchy.
Do keep copy calm, direct, specific, and easy to scan without reducing it to slogans.
Do use the supplied portrait and office photography as primary narrative material.
Do reserve serif scale for emotionally important statements and questions.
Do preserve visible keyboard focus, semantic controls, descriptive image alternatives, and reduced-motion behavior.
donts: Don't introduce generic wellness cards, rounded containers, floating badges, or decorative blobs.
Don't scatter iris across minor elements or add unrelated accent colors.
Don't use gradients as a substitute for daylight, photography, or material fields.
Don't invent testimonials, outcomes, pricing, insurance details, contact information, or credentials.
Don't turn the homepage's exact hero overlap or section sequence into a universal page template.
